clue.text: Computer article with flyer

blocks.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
the indefinite article
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone describes an item they read on a computer that came with a frequent-flyer offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large tropical parrot, so it is a bird and therefore a flyer.

clue.text: Base piece goes around base

indicators.note: going around something is surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A component wraps around the foot of a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: Both bases differ: the first is the adjective meaning low or ignoble, the second the mathematical constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and mean both describe something low, petty or ignoble in character.

clue.text: Pigeonhole character in remark

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: a comment is a remark
a part is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: A remark that typecasts someone, pigeonholing their character.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeonhole is a small separate section in a desk or rack, which is a compartment.

clue.text: Cordiality month after hostility

blocks.note: war is armed hostility
MTH is an abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Friendliness returns a month after a period of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Month after hostility' means the month comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth in manner is friendliness and affection, the same as cordiality.

clue.text: Reportedly uninterested following rodents around side of ship

indicators.note: turning around means the word for the rodents runs from its end back to its start
reportedly means as people say it, so the word for uninterested is taken by its sound
following puts the uninterested piece after the rodents piece, so it goes second

blocks.note: rats are rodents
bored means uninterested; a word spelt differently sounds the same

explanation.surface: Someone sulkily trails after rats as they scurry about the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed rodents come first because the second part is 'following' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel when facing forward.

clue.text: Sexy show Channel 4's invested in

indicators.note: something invested in another is put inside it

blocks.note: to show is to let someone see
a duct is a channel for fluid or cable
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Channel 4 has put money into a racy programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel 4' reads as the broadcaster but splits into a channel and the number four; 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seductive means alluring and tempting, close to sexy in describing attractiveness.

clue.text: A good crowd not up for hassle

indicators.note: not up says the word up itself is taken away from the crowd

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
a group is a crowd of people

explanation.surface: A decent crowd that is not up for any trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not up' looks like 'unwilling', but it removes the letters U and P from the crowd. AGGRO is British slang for trouble or bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for aggressive trouble or bother, which is hassle.

clue.text: Gap dentist regularly covers

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a blank is a gap or empty space
second, fourth and sixth letters of dentist

explanation.surface: A dentist routinely fills in gaps between teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like a verb for what the dentist does; it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blankets are bed covers, so covers is a plural noun matching the answer.

clue.text: Advanced exercise class for climber

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
PE is physical education, a school exercise class

explanation.surface: A higher-level fitness class designed for rock climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes are primates that clamber through trees, so a climber describes one loosely.

clue.text: Analysis of detectives department

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
a section is a department of an organisation

explanation.surface: A report examining the workings of the police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissection is a close examination of something piece by piece, a detailed analysis.

clue.text: Esteemed message in broadcast

indicators.note: in places the short message inside the word for broadcast

blocks.note: a programme broadcast has been aired
DM is a direct message on social media

explanation.surface: A respected message is read out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed and admired are synonyms, both meaning held in high regard.

clue.text: Shave fleece of rebellious sheep, perhaps

indicators.note: fleece is the outer coat, so only the outside letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: to graze is to touch or scrape lightly in passing, as a near shave does
first and last letters of rebellious

explanation.surface: An instruction to shear the wool off unruly sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like the sheep's wool to be shaved; it is the signal to take only the outside of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep feed by grazing, so they are an example of grazers, which the 'perhaps' acknowledges.

clue.text: Worker I see learned revolutionary way

blocks.note: a worker ant
taken as written
to clock is slang for to notice or see
learned and wise both mean knowledgeable

explanation.surface: A worker realises the scholarly way to bring about a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' points at political upheaval, but here it is about turning in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticlockwise names a direction of rotation, the way a wheel turns against the hands of a clock.

clue.text: Priceless lie best man and I concocted

indicators.note: concocted means made up from mixed ingredients, so the letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The best man and I invented a wonderful fib for the wedding speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inestimable is too valuable to be measured, which is what priceless means.

clue.text: Garments of kit worn by husband with game coming up

indicators.note: something worn by another surrounds it, so the kit encloses the others
in a down clue coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: a strip is a sports team's kit
H is the abbreviation for husband
solo is a card game, solo whist

explanation.surface: A husband wears clothes from a sports kit as a match approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' tempts as POLO itself, which is in the answer, but polo comes from reversing SOLO plus the P of the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo shirts are short-sleeved collared tops, so they are garments.

clue.text: Curse go-cart now and then ending in bush

indicators.note: now and then means only at intervals, so every other letter is kept
ending in asks for the last letter of the following word

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of gocart
last letter of bush

explanation.surface: A driver swears every so often after the go-cart ends up in a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word, so oath and curse are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: One pint drunk with mate that's anxious

indicators.note: someone drunk is muddled, so the letters given are jumbled

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single pint drunk with a friend who is fretting to get home.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious to get something done means being eager for it now, which is to be impatient.

clue.text: People easily persuaded to linger feeding cat

indicators.note: feeding puts food into a mouth, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: puss is a cat
to hover is to linger close by

explanation.surface: Soft-hearted people are talked into staying around to feed the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is someone who is easily influenced or beaten, so pushovers are easily persuaded people.

clue.text: Monster's child strangling Greek character

indicators.note: strangling wraps hands around a neck, so one piece closes around the other

blocks.note: a minor is a child in law
tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A monster's offspring throttles a figure from Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur was the bull-headed monster of Greek myth kept in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Internet users consuming electronic quips

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing something up, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: people who go online
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: People on the internet lapping up witty remarks sent electronically.
explanation.definitionFit: One-liners are short jokes delivered in a single sentence, so they are quips.

clue.text: Name of German man ignored in cushioned seat

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that word is dropped from the seat

blocks.note: an ottoman is an upholstered seat without a back
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A German fellow is left alone, ignored on a padded couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name of German man' reads as one phrase, but 'man' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German first name, as in Otto von Bismarck.

clue.text: Cork unfinished wine saved for later

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for cork is missing

blocks.note: to cork a bottle is to stop it
red is wine

explanation.surface: Putting the cork back in a half-drunk bottle of wine to keep for another day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stored has been put away and kept for future use, saved for later.

clue.text: Bop and twerk? It couldn't get any worse

definitions.note: a description of the state rather than the verb phrase itself

blocks.note: to bop someone is to hit them
twerking is a dance that rocks the bottom, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Dancing the bop and twerking: a low point in someone's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bop' looks like a dance alongside twerk, but it means strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit rock bottom is an idiom for reaching the lowest possible point, after which things cannot worsen.

clue.text: With initial lowering, craft puts down

indicators.note: in a down entry lowering a letter moves it further down, so the first letter goes to the bottom

blocks.note: craft and skill both mean expertise

explanation.surface: A craft with its leading edge dipping, as a plane comes down.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the craft word moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down an animal is to kill it, so the phrase is a euphemism for kills.

clue.text: Second-hand American edition

blocks.note: US is short for American
ed is an abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A pre-owned copy of the American edition of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods have had a previous owner, which is what second-hand means.

clue.text: Artist requiring help in conflict with a great master

indicators.note: things in conflict are at odds and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter needs assistance in a dispute with one of the Old Masters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay's RA; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was an Italian Renaissance painter, ranked among the Old Masters of European art.

clue.text: Standard box missing top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so that letter is lost

blocks.note: to spar is to box

explanation.surface: A regulation-size box that has lost its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container but is the verb to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected level, as in 'up to par', so it means standard.

clue.text: Parisian's in with French revolutionary wanting Pierre's clothes

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the named first name is taken off the revolutionary

blocks.note: en is French for in
Maximilien Robespierre, leader of the French Revolution's Terror
the part removed

explanation.surface: A Parisian joins a revolutionary but wants Pierre's garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun after Pierre's, but it is the verb meaning dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrobe someone is to dress them in a robe, so the verb clothes is a synonym.

clue.text: Revelations gentleman really likes to hear

indicators.note: to hear means the phrase is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman
to prize something is to value it greatly

explanation.surface: A list of the things a gentleman truly enjoys being told.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprises are unexpected things that come to light, so revelations in a loose sense.

clue.text: Fear about being restricted by patriarch

indicators.note: being restricted by means being hemmed in, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a father is the patriarch of a family
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A family's fears about being kept in check by its domineering head.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, so the two are synonyms.
